links.outcome: LLM robustness to lexical, syntactic, and adversarial prompt perturbations on MedMCQA
links.effect: Models resilient to simple lexical substitutions or paraphrasing but break down under syntactic reordering or misleading contextual cues; fragility across general-purpose and medical LLMs. No numbers in abstract.
links.quote: While models tend to show resilience to simple lexical substitutions or paraphrasing, they often break down under syntactic reordering or misleading contextual cues.

links.outcome: Consistency of LLM responses across equivalent reworded prompts
links.effect: Even minor variations in phrasing can alter clinical advice; models can change diagnoses due to reworded inputs. No numbers in abstract.
links.quote: Even minor variations in phrasing can alter clinical advice, and targeted adversarial prompts can provoke harmful outputs.

screen.reason: Evaluates LLM robustness and sensitivity to prompt perturbations/adversarial prompts on a medical QA benchmark (MedMCQA) without evaluating a specific deployment guardrail or practice.
